clue.text: Being part of choir a fascinating, uplifting, wild experience

indicators.note: in a down entry, lifting something up means reading it from bottom to top, so backwards
only a portion of the following run of words is wanted, so the letters lie inside them

parts.note: the letters spanning the end of choir, the word a and the start of fascinating

explanation.surface: Singing in a choir is described as a thrilling, uplifting and exhilarating experience.
explanation.walkthrough: The hidden run IRAFAS, read upwards, gives SAFARI.
explanation.definitionFit: A safari is an expedition to watch big game in the African bush, an untamed adventure.

clue.text: Obscure papers concealed by ambassador

indicators.note: something concealed by another thing is wrapped inside it

parts.note: HE, His Excellency, is the formal style of an ambassador
identity papers

explanation.surface: Secret documents are being kept hidden by a diplomat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Obscure' looks like an adjective but works as the verb. His Excellency is the formal title of an ambassador.
explanation.definitionFit: To obscure something is to conceal it from view, which is what hiding does.

clue.text: I love Ms Kournikova investing in Greek city

indicators.note: to invest is to clothe or surround, so the name wraps around the following word

parts.note: taken as written
love is zero in tennis scoring, the letter O
Anna Kournikova, the Russian tennis player
taken as written

explanation.surface: A fan declares affection for Anna Kournikova as she puts money into a Greek city.
explanation.walkthrough: Love is zero in tennis, a nice fit with the tennis star in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Ioannina is a city in the Epirus region of northwestern Greece, on Lake Pamvotida.

clue.text: Garment made of piece of cloth that's mostly light

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all of the word is used, so its final letter goes

parts.note: a rag is a scrap of cloth
to light, as a bird lights on a branch, is to land or alight

explanation.surface: A garment is made from a cloth that is mostly lightweight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Light' looks like an adjective about weight but is the verb meaning settle or come down. LAND loses its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A raglan is an overcoat whose sleeves run in one piece up to the collar, named after Lord Raglan.

clue.text: It'll wake me up like loud music around 11:50, which is totally pointless

parts.note: a la, in the style of

indicators.note: around means the music wraps itself about the time that follows

parts.note: rock is loud music
with the colon's points removed this is 1150, MCL in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Someone grumbles about being woken by blaring music just before midnight, which seems utterly pointless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Totally pointless' tells you to drop the dots of the colon, so 11:50 becomes the number 1150, which is then written in Roman numerals.
explanation.definitionFit: An alarm clock is the bedside timepiece set to ring and rouse a sleeper at a chosen hour.

clue.text: Spanish operetta can be one's dish

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a traditional Spanish light opera mixing song and spoken dialogue
second meaning: a Catalan seafood stew

explanation.surface: A light opera from Spain might be just what someone fancies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One's dish' plays on the idiom for something you like; the second meaning is a literal dish, a Spanish fish stew of the same name.
explanation.definitionFit: Zarzuela names both the Spanish genre of comic musical theatre and a rich Catalan stew of mixed seafood.

clue.text: Boatman adrift around island somewhere across the pond

indicators.note: around means the jumbled letters enclose the following single letter
something adrift has broken loose and wanders, so these letters drift out of order

parts.note: taken as written
I is the abbreviation for island

explanation.surface: A boatman lost at sea drifts round an island somewhere on the far side of the Atlantic.
explanation.walkthrough: BOATMAN rearranged as MAN-TOBA takes I into its middle. 'Across the pond' means in North America, seen from Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Manitoba is a Canadian province, and Canada lies over the Atlantic Ocean from Britain.

clue.text: Maybe copies of Graceland are worthless in Lesotho

parts.note: an are is a metric unit of area, abbreviated A

indicators.note: in means the word sits inside the country's abbreviation

parts.note: the international country code for Lesotho; it wraps the next piece
bum, as an adjective, means of poor quality

explanation.surface: Copies of Paul Simon's Graceland, made with southern African musicians, are said to be valueless in Lesotho.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Are' is not the verb but the metric unit of land area, a hundred square metres.
explanation.definitionFit: Graceland is a Paul Simon LP, so copies of it are examples of records, hence the question-like 'Maybe'.

clue.text: Bright composer, finishing early, to return before noon

indicators.note: returning means going back the way it came, so the shortened name is read backwards
stopping before the end means the name's last letter is cut off

parts.note: Sir Edward Elgar, the English composer
AM, ante meridiem, is the time before noon; the link word places it after

explanation.surface: A clever composer leaves work early to come back in the morning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Before noon' reads as one phrase but splits: before is only placing, and noon stands for the hours ahead of midday.
explanation.definitionFit: Agleam means shining or glowing with light, a literary word for something bright.

clue.text: Informed women to get out of that Swiss river

indicators.note: getting out of a word means leaving it, so that letter is removed

parts.note: aware means informed
W is the abbreviation for women

explanation.surface: Knowledgeable women are told to climb out of a Swiss river.
explanation.walkthrough: AWARE without W leaves AARE.
explanation.definitionFit: The Aare is the longest river wholly within Switzerland, flowing through Bern into the Rhine.

clue.text: No voting system in Caribbean country should get an award

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the country should get, that is take in and hold, the voting system

parts.note: Belize, in Central America on the Caribbean coast
PR, proportional representation

explanation.surface: A Caribbean nation without a proper voting system is told it deserves a prize anyway.
explanation.walkthrough: Belize is in Central America but its coast is on the Caribbean, and it counts as a Caribbean nation.
explanation.definitionFit: The Nobel Prize is an international honour given yearly for peace, literature and the sciences.

clue.text: Composer, I understand, residing in Long Island

indicators.note: someone residing in a place lives inside it, so the phrase goes inside the abbreviation

parts.note: LI is the abbreviation for Long Island
'I get' means I understand

explanation.surface: A composer apparently lives on Long Island, as far as the speaker knows.
explanation.walkthrough: I GET goes inside LI.
explanation.definitionFit: György Ligeti was a Hungarian-Austrian composer, known for pieces used in the film 2001.

clue.text: Where one is struggling to become president

indicators.note: struggling suggests thrashing about, so the letters writhe into new places

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone describes the state of struggle you go through on the way to the presidency.
explanation.definitionFit: Dwight D. Eisenhower was the 34th President of the United States, after commanding Allied forces in Europe.

clue.text: Name the woman soundly beaten by Steffi at Wimbledon in 1992

indicators.note: soundly here means by sound, so what is said is wanted, not how it is written

parts.words: the woman soundly beaten by Steffi at Wimbledon in 1992
parts.note: Steffi Graf beat Monica Seles in the 1992 Wimbledon final

explanation.surface: A quiz question asks for the player Steffi Graf crushed in the 1992 Wimbledon final.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soundly beaten' reads as a thrashing, but 'soundly' is the sound signal. Spoken without a final R, as in standard British English, the two words match.
explanation.definitionFit: Monicker, or moniker, is an informal word for a person's name or nickname.

clue.text: One constantly talking German when appropriate

parts.note: G is the abbreviation for German
as means when, as in 'as he left'
to bag is to appropriate or seize

explanation.surface: A German is described as a chatterbox whenever it suits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Appropriate' looks like the adjective suitable but is the verb meaning take.
explanation.definitionFit: A gasbag is an informal word for a person who chatters on endlessly.

clue.text: Little sucker's obsession with the environment

parts.note: green means concerned with the environment
a bug is a craze or obsession, as in the travel bug

explanation.surface: A tiny baby's fixation on ecology is being described.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Little sucker' sounds like an affectionate name for a baby; it is a sap-sucking insect.
explanation.definitionFit: A greenbug is a small aphid that sucks the sap of cereal crops, so a tiny feeding pest.

clue.text: Traveller on street finds tissue

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street
the Roma are a travelling people; in an across clue 'on' puts this after

explanation.surface: A traveller walking along a street comes across some tissue.
explanation.definitionFit: Stroma is the supporting connective tissue framework of an organ, as distinct from its working cells.

clue.text: Juliet married a prince after retreating at a mausoleum

indicators.note: something retreating goes backwards, so the little word is read in reverse

parts.note: taken as written
Juliet is J in the radio alphabet
M is the abbreviation for married
taken as written
Prince Hal, the young Henry V in Shakespeare

explanation.surface: Juliet wed a prince after falling back, as if at a romantic mausoleum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' tells you the reversed little word comes first in the down entry. Prince Hal is Shakespeare's name for the young Henry V.
explanation.definitionFit: The Taj Mahal at Agra is the white marble tomb Shah Jahan built for his wife Mumtaz Mahal.

clue.text: French city is annoying

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a city in the Loire valley of western France

explanation.surface: Someone complains that a particular French city irritates them.
explanation.definitionFit: Angers is a historic city in Maine-et-Loire, and the verb form means irritates or provokes rage.

clue.text: A series of Holbein paintings makes one feel severely uncomfortable

indicators.note: a series is a run of consecutive items, so a run of letters is taken straight from the words

parts.note: the end of Holbein joined to the start of paintings

explanation.surface: Looking at a whole run of Holbein's pictures leaves a viewer acutely uncomfortable.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in pain is suffering hurt, a strong form of physical discomfort.

clue.text: Heroic tale about, yes, Spanish tennis player

indicators.note: about can mean turned round, so the tale is read backwards

parts.note: a saga is a heroic tale
si is Spanish for yes

explanation.surface: A grand story told about a Spanish tennis player, to which the answer is yes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spanish tennis player' looks like a single phrase, but Spanish belongs with yes, and the player is American.
explanation.definitionFit: Andre Agassi is an American former world number one who won eight Grand Slam singles titles.

clue.text: English landscape gardener who often joins 2 in conversation

definitions.meaning: first meaning: Gertrude, the influential garden designer
second meaning: Stevenson's doctor, paired in speech with the entry at 2

explanation.walkthrough: 2-down is HIDE, which said aloud is Hyde; people speak of Jekyll and Hyde. 'In conversation' covers both the pairing in talk and the sound match.
explanation.definitionFit: Gertrude Jekyll designed hundreds of English gardens, and Dr Jekyll is the respectable half of Stevenson's split personality.

clue.text: See about US lawyer leaving African country for Swiss town

indicators.note: about here means surrounding, so the exclamation wraps the shortened country

parts.note: lo, an old word meaning look or see

indicators.note: the lawyer leaving means those letters depart from the country's name

parts.note: Uganda in East Africa
DA, district attorney

explanation.surface: An American lawyer quits an African country for a Swiss town, and you are asked to look into it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' is the old exclamation lo, as in 'lo and behold'.
explanation.definitionFit: Lugano is a lakeside town in the Italian-speaking canton of Ticino in southern Switzerland.

clue.text: Nothing to add now, perhaps ring back later — 31 January 2020, say?

parts.note: 'end of' is a British slang way of closing an argument: there is no more to say

indicators.note: going back means reading the word from its last letter to its first

parts.note: a boxing ring is an example of an arena

explanation.surface: A curt phone message: nothing more to say right now, maybe call back later.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a phone call, but 'ring back' splits: ring is an arena, reversed. 31 January 2020 was the day the UK left the European Union.
explanation.definitionFit: Brexit day marked the close of nearly fifty years of British membership of the EU, a historic turning point.

clue.text: Russian novelist accommodates grand Irish dancer

indicators.note: to accommodate is to give room to, so the novelist's name houses the letters that follow

parts.note: Nikolai Gogol, author of Dead Souls
G is short for grand, a thousand pounds
IR is the abbreviation for Irish

explanation.surface: A Russian writer puts up a great Irish dancer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Irish dancer' looks like one phrase but splits: Irish is wordplay and dancer alone is the definition. A grand is slang for a thousand pounds.
explanation.definitionFit: A go-go girl is a young woman employed to dance energetically at a nightclub or discotheque.

clue.text: See 24
Pimps not supporting those who make things better

indicators.note: not here means without, so a word is taken away from the front

parts.note: a procurer obtains prostitutes for clients
pro means in favour of

explanation.surface: Pimps refuse to back the people who try to fix things.
explanation.walkthrough: PROCURERS loses PRO from the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Curers are healers who restore people to health, or remedy whatever is wrong.

clue.text: S? Part of Scarborough or Southport?

parts.note: surface reading: a lone letter followed by a question mark, as if asking what it stands for
setter's reading: S is the first letter, the leading edge, of the word for the ocean

explanation.surface: A puzzler wonders what the letter S might signify, perhaps a district of a seaside resort.
explanation.walkthrough: S is the front of SEA, and both Scarborough and Southport are English seaside towns with a promenade by the beach.
explanation.definitionFit: The seafront is the stretch of a coastal town facing the sea, a feature of every resort.
